title: Possible Interaction of Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs Against NF-kappaB- and COX-2-Mediated Inflammation: In Silico Probe.
authors: Vardhini, Srinivasan Parvatha; Sadiya, Heena; Beigh, Saba; Pandurangan, Ashok Kumar; Srinivasan, Hemalatha; Anwer, Md Khalid; Waseem, Mohammad
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接评估NSAIDs与COX-2及NF-kappaB等炎症蛋白的结合，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且未涉及TF-DNA结合机制，仅方法上可部分借鉴。
abstract: In recent years, inflammatory mediators have been considered a possible key for nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID's). NSAID's have been known as most promising medication against inflammation and its mediated pain. Inflammation could be recognize as a systemic adaptive stimulation triggered by detrimental stimuli as pathogenic attack and endogenous signals mediated injury inside the cells. In addition, there has been an inflammatory key mechanism involved in disease state. NSAIDs have been compromisingly recommended for targeting specific proteins and/or inflammatory-mediated enzymes including cyclooxygenases (COX). This subsequently inhibits the prostaglandins at the site of inflammation. For the past decades, two forms of the COX enzyme have been implicated as COX-1 expressed in cells and tissues and other COX-2 selectively triggered via proinflammatory cytokines at the site of inflammation and/or injury. In addition, NSAID's have also been implicated for the inhibition of NF-kappaB pathways, and other relevant proteins considered potent candidates for these drugs. NF-kappaB has been identified a classical proinflammatory signaling pathway. It has been recognized as a primary target for novel anti-inflammatory drugs. In our results, reports are being confirmed via the probable effects of NSAID's on inflammatory-mediated switches. Several studies were considered to enquire the possible interactions of NSAID's and inflammatory hub. Nevertheless, the exact mechanism is still debatable. In our study, NSAID's and their targeted proteins or molecules caused a convincing pattern. For improvised perception, the binding affinity of NSAID's with inflammatory-mediated proteins was quantified using a molecular docking tool. In addition, we have depicted the complex juncture of hydrogen bonding in targeted proteins with NSAID's. Our in silico investigations have revealed NSAID's as the powerful armor against COX-2- and NF-kappaB-mediated inflammation.
abstract_zh: 近年来，炎症介质被视为非甾体抗炎药（NSAID's）可能的关键靶点。NSAID's已被公认为对抗炎症及其介导疼痛的最有前景的药物。炎症可被识别为一种由有害刺激（如病原体攻击和细胞内源性信号介导的损伤）触发的系统性适应性刺激。此外，疾病状态中涉及一种炎症关键机制。NSAID's已被推荐用于靶向特定蛋白质和/或炎症介导的酶，包括环氧化酶（COX）。这随后在炎症部位抑制前列腺素的生成。过去几十年中，COX酶的两种形式已被涉及：COX-1在细胞和组织中表达，而COX-2则通过炎症和/或损伤部位的促炎细胞因子选择性触发。此外，NSAID's也被认为抑制NF-kappaB通路及其他相关蛋白质，这些被认为是这些药物的潜在候选靶点。NF-kappaB已被确定为经典的促炎信号通路，并被视为新型抗炎药物的主要靶点。在我们的结果中，报告通过NSAID's对炎症介导开关的可能效应得到确认。多项研究探讨了NSAID's与炎症枢纽的可能相互作用，然而确切机制仍有争议。在我们的研究中，NSAID's及其靶向蛋白质或分子呈现出令人信服的模式。为改进理解，我们使用分子对接工具量化了NSAID's与炎症介导蛋白质的结合亲和力。此外，我们描绘了靶向蛋白质与NSAID's之间氢键连接的复杂节点。我们的计算机模拟研究揭示，NSAID's是对抗COX-2和NF-kappaB介导炎症的强大武器。
